source_refs.note: Topic 12.5.2 with Figures 12.4 and 12.5, printed pages 277-278.

blocks.text: NOx takes part in a series of reactions leading to ozone, aldehydes, peroxyacyl nitrates (PANs) and peroxybenzoyl nitrate (PBN). PAN is one member of the peroxyacyl nitrates, general structure RC(O)OONO2 (Figure 12.4); in peroxyacetyl nitrate R is CH3, but other hydrocarbon chains may be present. The formation of PAN (Figure 12.5): the main component of oxidising smog is ozone, which oxidises a hydrocarbon to an aldehyde; the aldehyde reacts with a hydroxyl radical to give an acyl radical; the acyl radical reacts with oxygen to give a peroxyacyl radical, which finally reacts with nitrogen dioxide to form peroxyacyl nitrate.

blocks.caption: Mechanism of PAN formation (Figure 12.5)
rows: O3 oxidises the hydrocarbon RCH3 to the aldehyde RCHO
RCHO + HO. gives the acyl radical RC(=O).
RC(=O). + O2 gives the peroxyacyl radical RC(=O)OO.
RC(=O)OO. + NO2 gives RC(=O)OONO2, peroxyacyl nitrate (PAN)

blocks.prompt: What does PAN stand for, give its general formula, and name the compounds responsible for its formation (Quick Check 12.2b, c).
blocks.explanation: Peroxyacyl nitrate (peroxyacetyl nitrate when R = CH3), general formula RC(O)OONO2. It forms from hydrocarbons (VOCs) oxidised by ozone to aldehydes, hydroxyl radicals, oxygen and nitrogen dioxide, all generated in sunlit air containing NOx.

items: PAN = peroxyacyl nitrate RC(O)OONO2 (R = CH3 in peroxyacetyl nitrate); formed from aldehyde (hydrocarbon + O3), HO. radical, O2 and NO2 via acyl and peroxyacyl radicals.
